facts.raw_span: a 3-year history of nonhealing crusted scalp lesions
Previous treatments with various topical glucocorticosteroids and antibiotics showed no improvement
occasional otitis media
The family history was negative for skin disease
Multiple disseminated erythematous papules, petechial hemorrhages, and yellowish crusts were present on the scalp
Neck, axillary, and inguinal lymph nodes showed no abnormalities
Routine blood examinations revealed no pathological findings
Two osteolytic lesions identified on the right frontoparietal skull
Subepidermal infiltrate consisting of large cells with kidney-shaped nuclei, solitary lymphocytes, and eosinophilic granulocytes
The infiltrate stained positively for CD1A
Ultrasonography of abdomen and lymph nodes: normal
Serum electrophoresis: normal

concepts.why: The presence of nonhealing crusted scalp lesions, erythematous papules, and petechial hemorrhages, along with the pathological findings of subepidermal infiltrate consisting of large cells with kidney-shaped nuclei and positive staining for CD1A, are consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
The presence of osteolytic lesions and subepidermal infiltrate consisting of large cells with kidney-shaped nuclei are consistent with histiocytosis.
The presence of osteolytic lesions and eosinophilic granulocytes in the subepidermal infiltrate are consistent with eosinophilic granuloma.

The presence of multiple disseminated erythematous papules, petechial hemorrhages, and yellowish crusts, along with the pathological findings, are consistent with multifocal Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
The presence of subepidermal infiltrate consisting of large cells with kidney-shaped nuclei and solitary lymphocytes are consistent with congenital self-healing reticulohistiocytosis.
The presence of subepidermal infiltrate consisting of large cells with kidney-shaped nuclei and solitary lymphocytes are consistent with indeterminate cell histiocytosis.
The presence of nonhealing crusted scalp lesions, erythematous papules, and petechial hemorrhages, along with the pathological findings, are consistent with proliferative histiocytosis.
The presence of subepidermal infiltrate consisting of large cells with kidney-shaped nuclei and solitary lymphocytes are consistent with Rosai-Dorfman disease.

rationales.F01: Nonhealing crusted scalp lesions suggest a chronic condition, which is more typical of Langerhans cell histiocytosis and multifocal Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
rationales.F02: Lack of response to topical treatments may indicate a more severe condition, such as Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
rationales.F05: The presence of disseminated erythematous papules, petechial hemorrhages, and yellowish crusts on the scalp is consistent with Langerhans cell histiocytosis and multifocal Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
rationales.F08: Osteolytic lesions are a characteristic feature of Langerhans cell histiocytosis, multifocal Langerhans cell histiocytosis, and eosinophilic granuloma.
rationales.F09: The presence of large cells with kidney-shaped nuclei, solitary lymphocytes, and eosinophilic granulocytes in the subepidermal infiltrate is highly suggestive of Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
rationales.F10: Positive staining for CD1A is a specific marker for Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of large cells with kidney-shaped nuclei, solitary lymphocytes, and eosinophilic granulocytes in the subepidermal infiltrate, along with the positive staining for CD1A, strongly supports Langerhans cell histiocytosis. The multifocal nature of the disease, with both scalp lesions and osteolytic lesions, is also consistent with this diagnosis.
